title: Anterior Versus Posterior Surgery for Eyelid Ptosis
official: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Anterior Versus Posterior Levator Aponeurosis Advancement for Eyelid Ptosis Correction
summary:
The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to compare two surgical approaches for correcting drooping of the upper eyelid (aponeurotic ptosis) in adults who need surgery. This condition occurs when the tissue connecting the eyelid-lifting muscle to the eyelid becomes weakened or detached. It can affect one or both eyes.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Does surgery performed through the inner surface of the eyelid (posterior approach) achieve an upper eyelid height at 6 months that is not meaningfully worse than surgery performed through the skin (anterior approach)?
* How do the two approaches compare in terms of complications, operating time, swelling, bruising, eyelid appearance, and patient satisfaction?
* How stable are the results during the 6 months after surgery?

Researchers will compare anterior and posterior approaches to levator aponeurosis advancement, a procedure that repositions and reattaches the tissue connecting the eyelid-lifting muscle to the eyelid. Both approaches are routinely used at Hospital Universitario 12 de Octubre in Madrid, Spain, where the study will take place.

Participants will be assigned by chance to one of the two surgical groups, with an equal chance of receiving either approach. All procedures will be performed under local anesthesia by the same experienced surgeon.

The main outcome is upper eyelid height 6 months after surgery, measured as the distance between the upper eyelid edge and the reflection of a light at the center of the pupil. The study will assess whether the posterior approach is no more than 0.5 millimeters worse than the anterior approach for this measurement. An independent healthcare professional will measure eyelid height and assess eyelid appearance.

Participants will:

* Attend a preoperative assessment, including an eye examination and measurements of eyelid position and movement.
* Undergo surgery using the randomly assigned approach.
* Attend follow-up visits the day after surgery, at 1 week, and at 1, 3, and 6 months.
* Have eyelid measurements and standardized photographs taken, and be assessed for swelling, bruising, and complications.
* Answer questions about their satisfaction with the appearance and function of their eyelids at 1, 3, and 6 months.

The visits and clinical assessments follow the hospital's usual care schedule for this surgery. Participation does not require additional visits or invasive tests beyond routine care.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults older than 18 years.
* Diagnosis of unilateral or bilateral aponeurotic ptosis caused by weakening or disinsertion of the levator aponeurosis.
* Clinical indication for surgical correction of ptosis.
* No previous ocular surgery.
* No other ophthalmic conditions that may affect eyelid anatomy.
* Provision of written informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Congenital, traumatic, neurogenic, myogenic, or mechanical ptosis.
* Previous eyelid surgery.
* Inability to provide informed consent or refusal to participate.
* Inability to cooperate with the surgical procedure under local anesthesia because of cognitive impairment or another disabling condition.
